messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need to decide KV cache residency/eviction policy for the trace KV store. Storage costs are rising and some queries spike miss latency.
jon: Short context? why now?
maria: We've got long-lived keys (30+d) that are rarely accessed for analytics but stay pinned, and the same store backs online enrichers used by runtime. Cost vs latency tradeoff.
anya: Is this the same prefix/KV cache the runtime uses for inference? mixing consumers sounds risky.
maria: Yes — two consumers: latency-sensitive online enrichers and batch analytics. They have different access patterns and cost impact.
sam: Quick proposal: add a "residency class" tag (hot/warm/cold) + tiered TTLs + probabilistic refresh for hot items. Hot pinned longer, cold evicted aggressively.
lee: How do we classify hot vs warm? by QPS rolling window? purely frequency is noisy.
maria: Combine access frequency + billing-impact signal. Example heuristic: high hits in last 6h AND contributes >X% of billing weight => hot.
jon: Need hysteresis to avoid oscillation when traffic shifts. E.g., require sustained drop > 12h before demote.
anya: Also consider attribution correctness: if we evict keys used to resolve cost buckets, queries fall back to expensive late-join paths and mis-attribute.
sam: Agreed. Add a sticky flag when a key has been used in billing resolution in the last 7 days; sticky keys get higher residency.
maria: Operational metrics to expose: eviction_rate_by_tier, miss_latency_p50/p95, attribution_fallback_rate, storage_bytes_by_tier.
lee: Add alert: attribution_fallback_rate > 0.5% for 15m -> page SRE.
jon: Migration question: if we shorten TTLs, analytics will see more misses and might backfill, causing load. Do we need a backfill plan?
maria: Plan I suggest: dry-run mode (mark classified values but don't evict) for 48h in canary region; then 50% traffic for 72h; then full rollout. Backfill script to pre-pin keys for enterprise tenants.
anya: For classification, propose a background job that recomputes residency every hour and writes a residency tag. Keep rules deterministic and simple.
sam: Pseudocode for classification we discussed:
```
// run hourly
if hits_last_6h > 100 and billing_cost_share > 0.05:
  residency = "hot"
elif hits_last_6h > 10:
  residency = "warm"
else:
  residency = "cold"
// apply sticky if used_for_billing_recently
if used_for_billing_in_7d:
  residency = max(residency, "warm")
```
jon: Need precise definitions for thresholds and the "max" operator — we should enumerate numeric values per tier in RFC.
lee: Also discuss eviction algorithm: LRU within each tier? or TTL-first with probabilistic early eviction to avoid hot bursts? LRU can thrash with fanout.
maria: I prefer TTL + LFU-ish bumping for hot keys. Implementation note: avoid scanning whole namespace; use per-shard counters and sampled movers.
anya: For reproducibility and audits, log residency transitions as events with reason codes (e.g., HTF=hit_threshold, BILL=used_in_billing).
sam: Config example for ops/proto: 
```
residencyRules:
  - name: hot
    min_hits: 100
    min_billing_share: 0.05
    ttl_secs: 604800
  - name: warm
    min_hits: 10
    ttl_secs: 86400
  - name: cold
    ttl_secs: 3600
hysteresis_secs: 43200
sticky_billing_days: 7
```
jon: We'll need a migration tool: one-off job to pin keys frequently used by billing for last 90d to avoid initial fallout.
maria: Ops runbook item: how to roll back — toggle dry-run flag -> reclassify -> rehydrate -> monitor metrics.
lee: Who owns the feature? eng-platform for classification + runtime-side guardrails; eng-runtime for client library changes.
anya: SGTM. I'll draft the RFC addendum covering thresholds, metrics, rollout steps, migration script, and runbook snippets.
sre-bot: deploy-check: canary env tests passed ✅
jon: Good — I'll author the RFC addendum and link the checklist, include the config proto and a simulation of expected cost delta.
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll open the PR for the classification job and the runbook link in the RFC.
lee: :thumbsup:
